title: Angle Between 3D Vectors
description:
Compute the angle in radians between two 3D vectors. First obtain their cosine:

$$
c=\frac{\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{w}}{\lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert_2\lVert\mathbf{w}\rVert_2}
$$

Then recover the angle:

$$
\theta=\arccos(c)
$$

Clamp $c$ to $[-1,1]$ before applying arccos to protect against floating-point error. If either vector has zero norm, the angle is undefined, so return np.nan. Otherwise return a Python float in $[0,\pi]$.

solution:
### 💡 Intuition & Approach
Computes the dot product divided by vector magnitudes and passes the clamped value into $\arccos$.

### ⚡ Python Reference Implementation
```python
import numpy as np

def angle_between_3d(v: list, w: list) -> float:
    v_arr = np.array(v, dtype=float)
    w_arr = np.array(w, dtype=float)
    dot = np.dot(v_arr, w_arr)
    norm_v = np.linalg.norm(v_arr)
    norm_w = np.linalg.norm(w_arr)
    if norm_v == 0 or norm_w == 0:
        return 0.0
    cos_theta = np.clip(dot / (norm_v * norm_w), -1.0, 1.0)
    return float(np.arccos(cos_theta))
```

- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
